newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GIANTS FACE UPHILL TASK TO QUALIFY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GIANTS FACE UPHILL TASK TO QUALIFY.

text.p: Manchester United manager Alex Ferguson was confident, Louis van Gaal of Ajax Amsterdam was uncertain but both their sides face the humbling prospect of a European Cup exit.
The two men watched their teams slump to home defeats in the Champions' League on Wednesday, casting considerable shadows over their presence in the quarter-final stages of the competition.
Those defeats, the second at home for each team, have left both clubs with the unenviable, uphill task of travelling away from home and effectively needing a win to qualify.
History is against both of them in the sense that no side has ever qualified for the latter stages of the competition after losing two home matches in the Champions' League.

Another giant whose place in the latter stages is by no means certain is Italian champions AC Milan whose away draw at Porto left them needing one point from their final showdown in Italy with Rosenborg Trondheim of Norway, to secure a quarter-final trip to Juventus.

For English champions Manchester United, who lost 1-0 in a thrilling match with European title-holders Juventus at Old Trafford, the equation is straightforward -- they need to win against Rapid Vienna on December 4.
The task is made slightly simpler by the fact that the Austrians have already been eliminated from the competition.

A draw would be enough if Juventus, who have already qualified impressively at the top of the group, beat Turkish club Fenerbahce in Turin because United came out one-goal better in their two clashes with the Turks.
But if Fenerbahce produce another upset similar to the one which saw them steal a surprise 1-0 win at Old Trafford, then it is curtains for United.
There was a suggestion that, with the hard work out of the way, the Italians might ease up in the final match but that idea was quickly scotched by Juventus coach Marcello Lippi.
"I can state categorically we will play in our usual manner and I hope sincerely that we will our final game," he said after Wednesday's game.
"There is no question that now we have qualified we will ease up against Fenerbahce. We do not play like that, we play to win."
Those were comforting words to Ferguson who appeared confident that his side could still qualify: "Juventus play to win every match out of habit, I know they will not ease up against the Turks.
"I am happy to go to Vienna knowing we must win. Now we have a great chance of going through. It is up to us to get a result in Vienna."

For Ajax, beaten by Juventus in the final last year, the job of qualifying is made more difficult by the fact that they are one of three teams on nine points and one of the others is Grasshopper Zurich, their final opponents.
The third team is French side Auxerre, who beat Ajax 2-1 on Wednesday, and they have the relatively simple task of hosting Glasgow Rangers.

In effect the match in Zurich is a straight winner-takes-all match although a draw could see both go through if Rangers follow their 2-1 win over Grasshopper with another win in Auxerre. Unlikely but not wholly impossible.
Van Gaal was hardly optimistic, though, and admitted that qualification for the quarter-finals would now be difficult.
"We're missing too much at the moment. We have most of the possession but we're creating too few chances," he said.
If Manchester United do qualify they will face Porto in the quarter-finals while Ajax, depending on how the group finishes, would meet either Atletico Madrid or Borussia Dortmund.
